text:
elena: Heads-up — planning to push the Dedicated GPU pool autoscale policy change today 16:30 UTC. PR here: https://git.internal/redwood/infrastructure/pulls/482
jack: I can be on the deploy. ETA 16:25 UTC to start the rollout window.
priya: What's the actual config delta? quick paste?
elena: main changes: lower min_gpus from 6 -> 3 for non-prod pools, add burst_capacity = 2, change scale_down_grace = 300s. I'll paste snippet:```
autoscale:
  min_gpus: 3
  max_gpus: 32
  burst_capacity: 2
  scale_down_grace_seconds: 300
  metric: queue_length_per_gpu
```
aaron: Is there a canary plan? we should validate KV cache eviction and tail-latency on the canary.
elena: yes — 10% traffic to pool "dedicated-eu-canary" for 20m, then 50% for 10m, then full. fallback route to hosted when errors > 2% or p50_gen_latency increases > 50ms.
jack: I'll run the canary and watch metrics. Please confirm smoke-check checklist.
priya: Smoke checklist: 1) canary model starts with full KV cache warmup (run warmup script) 2) check GPU_util 65-85% 3) queue_length < 8 4) p50 and p95 token latency within baseline 5) no new 5xxs in app logs
sasha: Adding: verify autoscaler controller logs for scaling decisions, and ensure burst tokens are consumed not exceeding policy.
elena: rollback readiness: we have the previous autoscale config in the config-store tagged v2026-03-12. Rollback is `infractl apply --config=autoscale-v2026-03-12` and then force-drain new pools. Jack, can your team run that if needed?
jack: yes. team on standby. I'll also keep a slack thread in #eng-oncall for immediate paging.
qa-bot: Automated smoke tests queued: test-suite/dedicated-pool-smoke v2. Expect results in ~8m after canary starts.
aaron: One more ask — PR needs a short note in rollout doc with metrics to observe and contact list. I can add it, elena can you add the expected thresholds?
elena: Added thresholds to PR description. Also left notes about cost impact (estimated +6% spend for the first 24h due to burst warmups).
priya: Code review ping @jack @sasha — approvals needed for the infra change.
sasha: Reviewing now. main question about burst_capacity: can we cap per-tenant bursts?
elena: Not in this change — that's a follow-up. This rollout is pool-level only; per-tenant bursts tracked in the backlog (issue #997).
jack: 16:22 UTC — warming canary nodes. infra-bot: deploy started for commit 3f8b9a.
infra-bot: canary-route: traffic_split=10% -> dedicated-eu-canary; autoscaler config applied.
elena: 16:35 UTC — canary live. starting smoke checks.
qa-bot: smoke tests: stage1 passed (connectivity, basic generate), stage2 running (latency/resolving).
priya: Observing p95 token latency +8ms compared to baseline, OK. queue_length steady at 3.
aar on: GPU_util 72% on canary, no scaling events yet.
jack: 16:48 UTC — bumping to 50% traffic for 10m as planned.
infra-bot: autoscaler observed spike -> +1 GPU on canary at 16:50 UTC (expected).
sasha: logs show scale decision due to queue_length metric, looks correct.
elena: No 5xxs, p50 stable. proceeding to full rollout in 5m if no regressions.
jack: 17:03 UTC — starting full rollout. will monitor for 30m.
priya: QA signals green.
qa-bot: full smoke suite passed on canary, and initial checks on full pool passing.
aaron: Monitoring dashboards alerted: small transient error spike at 17:06 (0.8%), recovered within 2 minutes. Not breaching rollback thresholds.
elena: Rollout complete at 17:20 UTC. Notes: autoscaler min reduced, burst enabled. tagging release: autoscale-policy-2026-03-17.
jack: Leaving final checklist: update runbook with new autoscale commands, inform finance about cost delta.
sasha: LGTM on the change.
elena: Thanks all. If anyone sees anomalies overnight, please ping #eng-oncall and tag @jack. :thumbsup:
